title: Claims and the wrong agency (fictional)
question: What happens when a claim goes to the wrong agency?
summary: An invented claims regulation and an invented draft bill for the fictional Commonwealth of Meridian. Follow a claim, see who owes which duty, and compare when the claim counts under each framework.
disclaimers: Meridian is fictional. This pack's regulation and draft bill were written for this demonstration and are not real law.
It does not describe the real electronic-filing bill or any real agency. The real bill pack is unavailable until its authentic text and dated official baseline sources are supplied.
Nothing here is legal advice or a calculation of anyone's real deadline.

scenarios.title: Complete claim to the responsible agency
scenarios.question: What happens when a complete claim reaches the right agency?
scenarios.summary: A claimant sends a complete claim, with a dollar amount, to the Department of Parks, which is responsible for the incident. Both frameworks present the claim on the same day and start the same six-month period.

scenarios.title: Complete claim sent to the wrong agency
scenarios.question: What happens when a claim goes to the wrong agency?
scenarios.summary: The claimant addresses a complete claim to the Department of Roads, but the Department of Parks is responsible. Roads forwards it one business day later. The baseline counts presentment from when Parks gets it. The draft keeps the original receipt time and gives Roads a two-business-day routing duty.

baseline.reasoning: § 14.2(b) imposes a transfer duty with no stated deadline; it is satisfied when performed.
§ 14.2(c): presented when Parks receives it, one business day later on 2 March 2027.

proposal.reasoning: § 4(a): two business days after Monday 1 March is Wednesday 3 March; forwarding on 2 March is on time.
§ 4(b) preserves the original receipt time, so presentment is 1 March 2027.
Six months from 1 March 2027.
No routing breach, so no complaint permission arises.

tour.title: The claim goes to the wrong agency
tour.body: The claimant addresses the claim to the Department of Roads. The Department of Parks is actually responsible.

tour.title: A two-day routing duty
tour.body: Under the draft, Roads must route the claim within 2 business days. This is a duty, not a promise that Roads will comply.

tour.title: The receipt time is preserved
tour.body: Section 4(b) treats the claim as received by Parks at the original receipt time.

tour.title: Why the date changes
tour.body: Under the baseline, presentment waits until Parks receives the claim. Under the draft it stays on the submission day. Compare the two frameworks to see the difference.

scenarios.title: Wrong agency misses the routing duty
scenarios.question: What if the wrong agency takes five business days to forward the claim?
scenarios.summary: Same claim, but Roads takes five business days. Under the draft the routing duty is breached and the claimant may complain, yet the preserved receipt time does not change. Under the baseline there is no deadline to breach, and presentment simply happens later.

scenarios.title: Claim without a dollar amount
scenarios.question: What happens when a claim omits the dollar amount?
scenarios.summary: The claim reaches the right agency but states no sum certain. The agency sends a notice after five business days and the claimant supplies the amount two weeks after filing. The draft does not clearly say whether the six-month period then runs from the original receipt time or from the cure, so this model leaves that unresolved until you choose a reading.

scenarios.summary: The Act is assumed enacted 60 days before the claim. Sections 3 and 4 are in effect after 30 days, but section 5 waits 180 days. So the receipt rule applies while the missing-amount notice duty does not yet operate.

scenarios.title: Intake system outage
scenarios.question: What happens when the electronic intake system is down?
scenarios.summary: The intake system is unavailable. Under the draft, the Claims Commission must offer another way to submit, and a submission that way counts when it is accepted. Under the baseline there is no electronic system, so the claimant mails a paper claim that counts when it arrives three business days later.

proposal.reasoning: § 7(a) requires an alternative; it has no stated deadline and is provided the same day.
§ 7(b): received when the alternative means accepts it on 2 March 2027.

glossary.plain: The moment a claim legally counts as made to the agency.
glossary.detail: In both fictional texts, a claim is presented when the responsible agency has it and it states a dollar amount. Presentment starts the six-month disposition period.

glossary.plain: When a submission first enters the intake system.
glossary.detail: Under the fictional draft, receipt does not wait for an employee to read the submission.

sourceRefs.quote: "Receipt time" means the time at which a submission first enters an intake system.

glossary.plain: Forwarding a claim from the wrong agency to the right one.
glossary.detail: The draft gives the wrong agency 2 business days. The baseline requires transfer but states no deadline.

sourceRefs.quote: shall route the claim to the responsible agency within 2 business days after the receipt time

glossary.plain: A specific dollar amount stated in the claim.
glossary.detail: Without a sum certain, neither fictional text treats the claim as presented.

glossary.detail: Section 5(b) of the fictional draft says a cured claim relates back to the original receipt time. Section 5(c) points the other way for the disposition period, so this model shows both readings.

sourceRefs.quote: the cured claim relates back to the original receipt time

glossary.plain: An option to act as if the agency said no, once six months pass without a decision.
glossary.detail: It is a permission for the claimant, not an automatic event and not a judgment on the merits.

sourceRefs.quote: the claimant may treat the failure as a final denial

glossary.detail: Meridian's holidays are invented for this demonstration.

presentment-direct.plain: The claim counts as presented on the day the responsible agency received it with a dollar amount.
presentment-direct.detail: Section 14.2(a) of the fictional regulation ties presentment to receipt by the responsible agency of a claim in a sum certain.

return-missing-amount.plain: The agency must return a claim that has no dollar amount.
return-missing-amount.detail: Section 14.4(a) states the duty but gives no deadline, so the model cannot record a late return as a breach.

transfer-duty.plain: The wrong agency must pass the claim on to the right agency.
transfer-duty.detail: Section 14.2(b) states the duty without a deadline. How fast the agency acts comes from a labeled assumption.

presentment-on-transfer.plain: The claim counts as presented only when the right agency receives it.
presentment-on-transfer.detail: Under § 14.2(c), the delay at the wrong agency pushes presentment later.

presentment-on-amount.plain: The claim counts as presented once it states a dollar amount.
presentment-on-amount.detail: Section 14.4(b) measures presentment from receipt of a claim with a sum certain.

disposition-clock.plain: A six-month period for the agency to decide starts at presentment.
disposition-clock.detail: The model counts six calendar months, not 180 days, and clamps to month end by assumption.

deemed-denial.plain: After six months without a decision, the claimant may treat the claim as denied.
deemed-denial.detail: This is an option for the claimant. It does not decide whether the claim succeeds.

mailed-claim.plain: A paper claim travels by mail before it counts.
mailed-claim.detail: The transit time comes from a labeled assumption, not from the regulation.

presentment-on-delivery.plain: The mailed claim counts when the responsible agency receives it.
presentment-on-delivery.detail: Section 14.2(a) ties presentment to receipt by the responsible agency.

receipt-time.plain: The claim is received the moment it enters the intake system.
receipt-time.detail: Section 3(a) of the fictional draft does not wait for an employee to read it.

act-presentment-direct.plain: The claim is presented at the receipt time.
act-presentment-direct.detail: Section 3(c) requires receipt by the responsible agency and a sum certain.

act-missing-amount-notice.plain: The agency must tell the claimant within 15 business days that the amount is missing.
act-missing-amount-notice.detail: Section 5(a) of the fictional draft. Section 5 takes effect 180 days after enactment.

routing-duty.plain: The wrong agency must route the claim within 2 business days.
routing-duty.detail: Section 4(a) creates a duty. Whether the agency actually meets it comes from a separate assumption.

preserved-receipt.plain: The claim keeps its original receipt time even though it went to the wrong agency.
preserved-receipt.detail: Section 4(b) treats it as received by the responsible agency at that time.

routing-complaint.plain: Because the routing deadline passed, the claimant may complain to the Claims Commission.
routing-complaint.detail: Section 4(d) permits a complaint. Section 4(c) says the receipt time stays the same.

cure.plain: Supplying the amount within 30 days cures the omission.

act-presentment-on-amount.plain: With the amount supplied, the claim is presented.

clock-relation-back.plain: Under reading A, the six-month period runs from the original receipt time.
clock-relation-back.detail: This follows § 5(b). Reading B, under § 5(c), would start it at the cure instead.

act-disposition-clock.plain: A six-month period for the agency to decide starts at presentment.
act-disposition-clock.detail: Section 6(a); § 5(c) says the period begins when the claim states a sum certain.

act-deemed-denial.plain: After six months without a decision, the claimant may treat the claim as denied.
act-deemed-denial.detail: Section 6(a) creates an option, not an automatic result.

alternative-means.plain: During an outage, the Claims Commission must offer another way to submit.
alternative-means.detail: Section 7(a) sets no time limit, so the model records the duty without a deadline.

alternative-receipt.plain: A submission through the alternative means counts when it is accepted.
